findings.message:
Shared Pages concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress: true` can cancel a deploy to `main`

The group `pages-${{ github.ref }}` resolves to `pages-refs/heads/main` for both a push to `main` and a `workflow_dispatch` on `main`. A newer run in that group cancels the run in progress. If a push run is in `deploy` (gated at [line 58](https://github.com/superyyrrzz/ForgeMap/blob/2f3977edabcb8fdf5f947704e727d798a46fe96f/.github/workflows/docs.yml#L58) to push on `main`) and someone starts a dispatch on `main`, the dispatch's `deploy` job is skipped. The cancelled commit is never published, and the site stays stale or mid-deploy until the next docs push. Back-to-back pushes to `main` have the same effect. The previous shared `"pages"` group with `cancel-in-progress: false` queued the later run instead. GitHub's Pages starter workflow uses `cancel-in-progress: false` for this reason; I could not check that offline. This change is also not mentioned in the PR description.

Fix: restore `cancel-in-progress: false`, or cancel only non-`main` runs with `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`.

Google Fonts loaded via CSS `@import` is render-blocking

The stylesheet previously had no external dependencies. The `@import` makes every page wait for a cross-origin CSS request to `fonts.googleapis.com` before its rules apply, then fetch woff2 files from `fonts.gstatic.com`. On cold connections this adds DNS, TCP, and TLS setup plus a round trip before first paint. `display=swap` does not help with the `@import` itself. The request also includes weights the stylesheet does not appear to use; for example, Outfit 400 and 500 are not referenced.

Fix: remove the `@import`, load the font stylesheet as a `<link rel="stylesheet">` in the page head with preconnect hints so it loads in parallel with `main.css`, and trim the requested weights. This needs a head partial or equivalent in the DocFX template.

Palette values are duplicated across tokens, RGB triplets, and literals

- The `--bs-*-rgb` triplets at lines 29, 31, 58, and 60 are hand-kept copies of the ember hex value.
- Literal `rgba(232, 118, 10, …)` values at lines 115, 120, 174, and 413 bypass the tokens.
- `--forge-ember-glow` is defined at lines 17 and 47 but never used.
- Token roles flip between modes. `--forge-ash` and `--forge-steel` are light in one mode and dark in the other, which forces hard-coded neutrals such as `#f4f1ed` (lines 102, 291) and `#e0ddd8` (line 238).

Changing `--forge-ember` leaves the glows and selection color on the old hue, and maintainers cannot tell which values are authoritative.

Fix: define one RGB triplet per mode (for example `--forge-ember-rgb: 232, 118, 10;`), derive `--forge-ember` and the `--bs-*-rgb` variables from it, write the alpha colors as `rgb(var(--forge-ember-rgb) / a)`, and either use or delete `--forge-ember-glow`.

Dark-mode search field renders as a light box with about 2.5:1 placeholder contrast

In dark mode, `--forge-steel-light` is `#c0bbb4` and `--forge-ash` is `#1a1f28`. The `header .form-control` rule uses both with `!important`, so the search field becomes a light box with dark text inside the always-dark navbar. The placeholder (`#6b7280` on `#c0bbb4`) measures about 2.5:1. Light mode has the inverse problem, with a dark field, and its placeholder is about 3.8:1. This assumes the DocFX search input is a `.form-control` inside `header`; I could not confirm that because the DocFX template sources are not in the repo.

Fix: give the field a mode-independent dark background and light text, or scope a `[data-bs-theme="dark"] header .form-control` override.

Dead `transition` on `.toc .nav-link`

Line 331 sets `transition: all 0.15s ease` on `.toc .nav-link`. The "Smooth theme transitions" group at lines 422–430 sets the same selector with the same specificity and no `!important`. The later shorthand replaces the earlier one, so line 331 never applies. The two hand-maintained lists have also drifted: `header .form-control` is in the reduced-motion list but has no transition, and `a` has a transition but is not listed there.

Fix: delete line 331, or remove `.toc .nav-link` from the group at line 430, and keep one owner for each transition.
